title: Heat loss through a composite wall
statement: A wall is plaster, brick and insulation in series. Its inside face is held at $T_1$ and its outside face at $T_4$. Find the heat loss $\dot{Q}$ through the wall.

figure.caption: The wall: plaster to $0.02\ \text{m}$, brick to $0.22\ \text{m}$, insulation to $0.27\ \text{m}$

steps.title: Read the wall
steps.note: Three layers in series between two faces at known temperatures. The table gives each layer's $L$ and $k$; the $R$ and $\Delta T$ columns are ours to fill.
steps.arabic: ثلاث طبقات على التوالي بين وجهين حرارتهما معلومة: الداخلي عند 20 درجة والخارجي عند −5 درجات. نحسب مقاومة كل طبقة ثم نجمع المقاومات.

steps.title: The other two layers
steps.note: The same rule for each: brick $\frac{0.20}{0.8 \times 1} = 0.25\ \text{K/W}$, insulation $\frac{0.05}{0.04 \times 1} = 1.25\ \text{K/W}$.

steps.title: Add them in series
steps.note: Layers in series add like resistors: $R_\text{total} = 0.04 + 0.25 + 1.25 = 1.54\ \text{K/W}$. The insulation carries most of it.

steps.title: Heat loss
steps.note: The whole temperature difference drives the heat through the total resistance: $\dot{Q} = \frac{T_1 - T_4}{R_\text{total}} = \frac{20 - (-5)}{1.54} = 16.2\ \text{W}$.
steps.arabic: فرق الحرارة الكلي $25\ \text{K}$ يدفع الحرارة عبر المقاومة الكلية، فيكون الفقد 16.2 واط.

steps.title: Check the temperature drops
steps.note: Each layer drops $\Delta T = \dot{Q} R$. The drops add back to the full $25\ \text{K}$, so the profile lands on $T_4$: the answer checks.

slips.note: The sheet's total row swaps two digits: its own layers add to $1.54$, and its heat loss uses $1.54$.
